body:
# Independent audit of the rank-sensitive continuous cover theorem

Audited `candidate a25f203b14ed76b3` against its
stated radial-integral and density-centerpoint dependencies. The proof
passes, including the external-contact density extension.

The orthogonal marginal has exactly the required negative-power
convexity: Brunn--Minkowski gives concavity of its positive
(D-r)-th root, and a decreasing convex power reverses the first
inequality and then supplies the second. Positive boundary slices
are retained. The compact-slice argument proves upper
semicontinuity, including dimension loss, and ordinary Fubini
preserves every cap mass without a Jacobian loss.

In the exterior case the strict separating coordinate satisfies
0<a<=t<=b. Thus the projected density is bounded and compactly
supported, has the exact Jacobian t^(r-1), and is upper
semicontinuous by reverse Fatou on the fixed compact t interval.
Its support and positive interior have the asserted convexity.
The radial lemma is invoked with p=r on the original r-dimensional
density, whose negative exponent is exactly -1/(r+1). Restriction
of the resulting convex extended gauge to (1,s) gives exponent
-1/r, precisely the density theorem's requirement in dimension
r-1. No log-concavity of the central projection is asserted or
needed. Empty and full projected restrictions are treated correctly.

The boundary-contact approximation translates the entire cover to
an exterior point. All limiting hyperplanes are Lebesgue-null for
the marginal density, so dominated convergence proves the original
closed-cap inequality. The equivalence between common-flat
intersection with int K and projected-contact membership in int B
is correct. The rank-one case is separately complete.

The ordinary sharpness product is exact. For the exterior rank-r
sharpness construction, use a simplex with centroid zero and
linear barycentric deviations beta_i.x=lambda_i(x)-1/r. With
0<epsilon<1/r, splitting beta_0 by +/-epsilon in the new t
coordinate gives largest cap fraction
((r-1)/r+epsilon)^(r-1). The positive weights 1,1,2,...,2
balance, and the two split normals together with the others span
rank r. Thus the displayed limit certifies sharpness with rank
exactly r. The same construction on 0<=t<=1 handles a boundary
contact. These normalization and small-epsilon conditions are
implicit in the note and can be stated explicitly for clarity.

No substantive gap was found. The final fiberwise statements
correctly retain a maximum over caps; they do not exchange that
maximum with a sum over integer fibers.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
